stories.headline: Nvidia in talks to guarantee about $250B of OpenAI financing for SoftBank's 10 GW Ohio campus

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI to lease a 10-gigawatt data-center project in southern Ohio, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, July 26.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is in talks to provide a roughly $250 billion backstop for OpenAI as part of a massive data-center project, one of the most ambitious financial transactions yet in America's artificial-intelligence boom. The guarantees from Nvidia would help the ChatGPT maker lease a 10-gigawatt project

key_facts.fact: The site is being developed by SB Energy, SoftBank's power subsidiary, in Pike County, southern Ohio, on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment facility roughly 50 miles south of Columbus; total cost including chips could exceed $500 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The backstop would enable OpenAI to lease a 10-gigawatt facility that SB Energy, SoftBank's power subsidiary, is building in southern Ohio. The project is sited on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment facility roughly 50 miles south of Columbus, and the full cost — including chips — could exceed $500 billion, making it the largest data center project announced to date.

key_facts.fact: The guarantee would cover the lease and construction debt but not the chips; separately Nvidia is discussing a structure to fund up to about $350 billion of OpenAI chip purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: The proposed guarantee would apply to the lease agreement and construction financing, but would not cover purchases of Nvidia's AI chips. In addition to the proposed guarantee, Nvidia is reportedly discussing a separate financing structure to support OpenAI's chip purchases, which the newspaper said could total around $350 billion.

key_facts.fact: The backstop is needed because OpenAI is not profitable and cannot obtain an investment-grade credit rating on its own, making lenders wary of the project's debt.
key_facts.excerpt: Such backing is needed partly because OpenAI has not yet turned a profit and therefore cannot obtain an investment-grade credit rating on its own. Terms have not been finalized and the deal could fall apart.

key_facts.fact: Power for the Ohio site is controlled by the US government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick deciding who gets access; Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also approached him about the site.
key_facts.excerpt: The power for the project is controlled by the U.S. government and funded separately by Japan under a recent trade deal, with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in deciding who will receive access to it... OpenAI, which has been in advanced talks for several weeks to lease the site, is among the companies showing the strongest interest in the project, while Anthropic, Microsoft and Google have also spoken to Lutnick in recent weeks

key_facts.fact: The first phase is expected to bring about 800 megawatts online in 2028; Nvidia has already invested $30 billion in OpenAI, after saying in September 2025 it would invest up to $100 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Power for the Ohio site is government-controlled, with allocation overseen by the US Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, and part of the supply funded by Japan under a trade agreement, so the first phase is expected to bring only around 800 megawatts online in 2028... In September 2025 Nvidia said it would invest up to $100bn in OpenAI as part of a partnership to deploy 10 gigawatts of its systems

stories.headline: China starts producing homegrown immersion DUV chip tools; ASML and equipment stocks tumble

key_facts.fact: A Shanghai-based, state-backed company has begun mass-producing immersion deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography tools for the first time, The Information reported on Monday, July 27, citing people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: A Chinese state-backed company has begun manufacturing one of the key pieces of equipment used in chip manufacturing for the first time

key_facts.fact: The unnamed Shanghai firm assembled DUV development teams from other Chinese companies, including state-backed startup Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology, and aims to build about five machines this year and roughly 20 next year.
key_facts.excerpt: A Shanghai-based company has started making immersion deep ultraviolet lithography tools, the Information reported on Monday... It has assembled development teams from other Chinese companies, including Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology for this... The unnamed Shanghai-based firm is seeking to make about five DUV machines this year and is targeting about 20 next year

key_facts.fact: First deliveries are expected to go to SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor and CXMT.
key_facts.excerpt: the state-backed machines are expected to be delivered later this year to leading Chinese semiconductor manufacturers, including Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. (SMIC), Hua Hong Semiconductor and ChangXin Memory Technologies.

key_facts.fact: ASML shares fell as much as 8.3% in Amsterdam to their lowest since early June; ASM International dropped as much as 7.3%, BE Semiconductor 9.9%, Applied Materials 6.7% and Lam Research 7.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock fell as much as 8.3%, having traded higher throughout the morning in Amsterdam. Jitters quickly spread to chip-equipment peers in Europe and the US: ASM International NV dropped as much as 7.3%, BE Semiconductor Industries NV slid 9.9%, Applied Materials Inc. declined 6.7% and Lam Research Corp. fell 7.9%.

key_facts.fact: The scale remains tiny next to ASML, which shipped 131 immersion DUV systems in 2025; Chinese tools still trail on performance and reliability and some key components are imported from Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML shipped 131 immersion DUV machines last year, showing the smaller scale of the Chinese production. Additionally, Chinese immersion DUV also imports some key components from Japan, while most are being sourced from China.

key_facts.fact: ASML is banned from selling EUV and its most advanced DUV machines to China under US-led export controls; China's share of ASML net system sales fell to 14% in Q2 from 19% in Q1.
key_facts.excerpt: China's contribution to ASML's net system sales fell to 14% in the second quarter from 19% in Q1. The declining share reflects both the tightening of export restrictions and the possibility that Chinese chipmakers are finding alternative supply.

stories.headline: CXMT jumps 466% on Shanghai debut, becoming China's most valuable listed company at ~$487B

key_facts.fact: Shares of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) closed at 49 yuan on their STAR Market debut on Monday, July 27, up 465.82% from the 8.66-yuan IPO price, with full-day turnover above 140 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) closed at 49 yuan (about 7.22 U.S. dollars) on its Shanghai STAR Market debut Monday, up 465.82 percent from its IPO price of 8.66 yuan, with full-day turnover surpassing 140 billion yuan.

key_facts.fact: The debut gave CXMT a market capitalisation of about 3.3 trillion yuan ($487 billion), overtaking Industrial and Commercial Bank of China as the most valuable company listed on mainland exchanges.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT's shares surged 466% in their first day of trading. The company has become the most valuable one listed on a mainland Chinese exchange, with an estimated market capitalization of about 3.3 trillion yuan (more than $487 billion). But that's still smaller than those of South Korean and American memory chipmakers like Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology.

key_facts.fact: The IPO raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion), rising to 66.61 billion yuan if the over-allotment is exercised — Asia's biggest listing of 2026 and the largest mainland semiconductor offering on record, ahead of SMIC's $7.5 billion sale in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT, formerly ChangXin Memory Technologies, raised 57.92-billion yuan (US$8.6-billion) in the IPO, the biggest mainland Chinese semiconductor offering on record. It surpasses SMIC's US$7.5-billion Shanghai share sale in 2020 and the IPO proceeds could rise to 66.61-billion yuan if an over-allotment option is fully used.

key_facts.fact: About 141.1 billion yuan of CXMT shares changed hands, the first A-share stock ever to exceed 100 billion yuan of turnover in a day; only 6.73% of the enlarged share capital was freely tradable at listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 141.1 billion yuan worth of CXMT shares were traded in Shanghai on July 27, making it the first A-share stock to exceed 100 billion yuan turnover in a day... Only 6.73 per cent of CXMT's enlarged share capital will be freely tradable at listing, as most shares are locked up.

key_facts.fact: CXMT expects first-half 2026 revenue of 110-120 billion yuan and net profit of 50-57 billion yuan, reversing a year-earlier loss; Q1 2026 revenue was 50.8 billion yuan, up more than 700% year on year.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT generated RMB50.8 billion in revenue in the first quarter of 2026, up more than 700% year on year, as demand for memory chips increased alongside AI server investment.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2016, CXMT makes DRAM and held roughly 8% of the global market as of June 2026, still about one generation behind Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2016, CXMT revealed its first DDR5 RAM products last year, though they currently remain 'roughly one generation' behind the top chips from Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, the South China Morning Post reports. As of June 2026, CXMT held an 8 percent share in the global RAM market, according to Counterpoint Research.

stories.headline: Samsung signs $200B chip pact with Broadcom as SK ties $750B of AI memory deals at Korea-US summit

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics said on Saturday, July 25 that it signed a memorandum of understanding with Broadcom covering memory, contract chipmaking and advanced packaging worth more than $200 billion through 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: [SEOUL] Samsung Electronics said on Saturday (Jul 25) it struck a pact with US chip designer Broadcom to widen cooperation across memory chips, contract chip making and advanced packaging envisaged to exceed US$200 billion until 2030.

key_facts.fact: The MOU was signed July 24 at a Korea-US AI summit in San Francisco and covers HBM4 and HBM4E memory supply plus 2-nanometer-and-below foundry production at Samsung's Pyeongtaek campus and 2.3D/2.5D advanced packaging.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal, announced on Friday at an AI summit in San Francisco, runs for five years through 2030... On the memory side, Samsung will supply Broadcom with next-generation high-bandwidth memory, including HBM4 and HBM4E chips, for use in Broadcom's AI accelerators. In foundry, Samsung will manufacture Broadcom products using two-nanometer and smaller process technologies at its campus in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.

key_facts.fact: The summit, convened by South Korean President Lee Jae Myung at The Midway in San Francisco on Friday, produced $950 billion in semiconductor and AI infrastructure commitments; SK Group committed to $750 billion of long-term supply partnerships, including a $500 billion-plus deal with Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung convened a high-stakes AI Summit at The Midway in San Francisco on Friday, yielding $950 billion in semiconductor and AI infrastructure commitments... Separately, SK Group committed to $750 billion in long-term memory chip supply partnerships with Nvidia and a broader coalition of US technology firms

key_facts.fact: SK's Nvidia partnership, estimated at more than $500 billion, covers AI-factory construction plus five-year memory supply and joint development of HBM4; the remaining $250 billion bundles other deals including AI-server memory supply to Microsoft.
key_facts.excerpt: the cooperation with Nvidia, estimated at more than $500 billion, includes long-term supply and joint development of next-generation AI memory such as HBM4. The remaining $250 billion is also the result of multiple big tech contracts bundled together, including mid- to long-term cooperation with Microsoft (MS) on memory supply for AI servers.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom had previously given Samsung only mature 8-nanometer work while sending leading-edge orders to TSMC; Samsung's foundry share is around 7% against TSMC's dominance, and its 2nm yields sit in the mid-50% range versus TSMC's 60-70%.
key_facts.excerpt: some sources place Samsung's 2nm yields in the mid-50% range, still short of the roughly 60% threshold the industry typically requires for stable mass production. TSMC, by comparison, is reportedly achieving 60 to 70% yield consistency at 2nm, and its foundry revenue share hit a record 70.2% in the second quarter of 2025. Samsung's share sat at 7.3%.

key_facts.fact: The agreement is an MOU, a statement of intent with no binding commitments on volume or price.
key_facts.excerpt: It is one of the largest semiconductor partnerships ever disclosed, though as an MOU it represents a statement of intent rather than a binding contract.

stories.headline: Nvidia invests in Ilya Sutskever's SSI, promising a 10x compute jump on Vera Rubin systems

key_facts.fact: Safe Superintelligence and Nvidia announced a long-term strategic partnership on Monday, July 27, including an Nvidia investment in SSI and access to the next-generation Vera Rubin platform, which the companies say will raise SSI's compute by an order of magnitude.
key_facts.excerpt: SANTA CLARA, Calif. and PALO ALTO, Calif., July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) and NVIDIA today announced a long-term partnership to rapidly accelerate SSI's strategic growth. NVIDIA has additionally made an investment in SSI. For SSI, NVIDIA's substantial investment combined with access to the next-generation, best-in-class NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform will allow SSI to increase its compute by an order of magnitude.

key_facts.fact: SSI said on X that the investment will let it '10x our compute in the next 12 months'; Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform reached full production this month.
key_facts.excerpt: "NVIDIA is making a substantial investment in SSI that will let us 10x our compute in the next 12 months," the company posted on X. The deal also gives SSI access to Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, which reached full production this month.

key_facts.fact: A source familiar with the deal told TechCrunch the investment stretches into multiple billions; Bloomberg reported Nvidia is set to invest $5 billion in cash.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's investment stretches into multiple billions, a source familiar with the deal told TechCrunch. Already an investor in SSI, the chipmaking giant said it signed this compute partnership to 'accelerate SSI's next stage of growth after obtaining rare access into the company's closely guarded research.'

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said it entered the partnership after obtaining rare access to SSI's closely guarded research, and the two will collaborate on the technical advancement of Nvidia's current and future compute platforms.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA entered this partnership to accelerate SSI's next stage of growth after obtaining rare access into the company's closely guarded research... The two companies will also collaborate on the technical advancement of NVIDIA's current and future compute platforms, leveraging SSI's unique insights into the future of AI.

key_facts.fact: Sutskever said: 'We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big NVIDIA computer will let us do so.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big NVIDIA computer will let us do so," said Ilya Sutskever, cofounder and CEO of SSI.

key_facts.fact: SSI, founded in 2024 and led by Sutskever and Daniel Levy, has raised roughly $3 billion at a $32 billion valuation from backers including Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, Greenoaks and Sequoia, and has no product or revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: SSI has operated largely behind closed doors since launching in 2024, but has already raised more than $3 billion at a valuation of $32 billion from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.

stories.headline: Enigma exits stealth with $71M seed and 100 robots anyone can control from a browser

key_facts.fact: Enigma, a robotics research lab less than a year old, emerged from stealth on Monday, July 27, with a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo's Conviction.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma, a research lab set to emerge from stealth on Monday, is taking a fundamentally different approach... To finance its mission, Enigma raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo of Conviction Partners.

key_facts.fact: The company put more than 100 of its own AI robots online, housed in hangars in Israel and California, for anyone in the world to control through a browser; the robots draw with paintbrushes, sword-fight each other and mix flasks in simple chemistry experiments.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma is launching a large-scale experiment that allows anyone in the world to interact online with more than 100 of its proprietary AI robots. These robots, housed in hangars located in Israel and California, can perform tasks such as drawing pictures with a paintbrush, fighting each other with swords, and performing simple chemistry experiments by picking up and mixing flasks with liquids.

key_facts.fact: Enigma says it built both the robotic arms and the underlying models from the ground up, and is studying how humans want to talk to robots — text, audio, video demonstrations or drag-and-drop — rather than only chasing model capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma claims to have developed both the robotic arms and their underlying models entirely from the ground up... 'Do we want to just talk to them over text or audio? Do we want to show them an example as a video? Or maybe do we want to tap, drag, and drop?'

key_facts.fact: It was founded by Jonathan Jacobi, Microsoft's youngest-ever employee, and Gal Niv; the two met in teenage hacking competitions and served together in Israel's Unit 8200.
key_facts.excerpt: Jonathan Jacobi (pictured right), Microsoft's youngest-ever employee — recruited by Wiz founder Assaf Rappaport during his time there — co-founded Enigma with his longtime friend Gal Niv (pictured left). The two met while competing in hacking competitions as young teens, then became close friends while serving together in Israel's elite Unit 8200

key_facts.fact: Enigma said on X that the round totalled $71 million and drew participation from researchers at OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, xAI, Cognition and Wiz.
key_facts.excerpt: Enigma raised a $71 million seed round led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with participation from Sarah Guo of Conviction Partners.

key_facts.fact: Jacobi argues current robots are too laborious to instruct: 'If you had to do your dishes and spent 15 minutes explaining to a robot where to put everything, everyone reaches the point of Forget it, I'll just do it myself.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'If you had to do your dishes and spent 15 minutes explaining to a robot where to put everything, everyone reaches the point of "Forget it, I'll just do it myself,"' Jacobi said. 'Right now, everyone is at that point — even with the most capable models.'

stories.headline: China's LimX Dynamics raises nearly $200M pre-IPO at $2.2B and shows an uncut autonomous chore demo

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based LimX Dynamics announced on July 25 the completion of a nearly $200 million pre-IPO financing round valuing it at RMB 15 billion (about $2.2 billion), bringing capital raised in the past six months to roughly $400 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Shenzhen-based company announced the completion of a nearly $200 million Pre-IPO financing round, bringing its total capital raised over the last six months to a staggering $400 million. The round, which values LimX at RMB 15 billion (approximately $2.2 billion)

key_facts.fact: New backers include IDG Capital, AI hardware manufacturer Lens Technology, the pan-European GGG Group, Redstone VC, WestSummit Capital and Hefei Binhu Industry Development Group; existing investors Stone Venture, SAIC's Shangqi Capital and NIO Capital stayed in.
key_facts.excerpt: New investors joining the cap table include IDG Capital, global AI hardware manufacturer Lens Technology, the pan-European GGG Group, Redstone VC, WestSummit Capital, and the Hefei Binhu Industry Development Group. Existing investors also doubled down. Stone Venture significantly increased its position, while automotive-backed funds such as Shangqi Capital (SAIC Motor) and NIO Capital maintained their support

key_facts.fact: Alongside the round LimX unveiled COSA 0.5, an agentic robot operating system, with a video of its Oli humanoid doing a room of household chores in a single uncut take with no teleoperation.
key_facts.excerpt: the company unveiled LimX COSA 0.5, the latest iteration of its agentic operating system, powering the Oli humanoid through an entire room of household chores in a single, uncut, and fully autonomous take.

key_facts.fact: LimX claims Oli is the first full-size humanoid in China to complete long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks in a home setting entirely autonomously; COSA uses a three-layer stack (whole-body motion control, vision-language-action skills, and an LLM/world-model cognitive layer) with the open-source FluxVLA Engine.
key_facts.excerpt: LimX claims this makes Oli the first full-size humanoid robot in China to successfully complete long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks in a home setting entirely autonomously... System 0: A foundational model handling the raw physics of whole-body motion control and balance. System 1: The skills layer... System 2: The cognitive layer, powered by large language and world models

key_facts.fact: The money will scale manufacturing of autonomous humanoids and expand commercial presence in Europe, the Middle East and Asia, as Chinese rivals Unitree and Deep Robotics move toward public listings.
key_facts.excerpt: the $200 million injection will be aggressively deployed to scale the manufacturing of fully autonomous humanoid robots and to expand LimX's commercial presence across key markets in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia... with competitors like Unitree and Deep Robotics already navigating fast-track approvals and profitable quarters
